assign.outcome:
**The scenes have weather now.** The slot model is untouched; every change is light, colour, a name, or a picture.

![the foyer](foyer-1920.png)

- **Every 3D link wears its name.** A canvas-texture **Sprite** — the theme's font, the ink/surface pair `.scene-tip` uses in 2D, the one pair that reads on a cream world and a near-black one with no branch. It faces the camera for free from any camera the chain declares, it *raycasts* (so a plate inside a linked group is part of the link, not a dead patch over it), and it is disposed by the slot that built it. [light](label-light.png) / [dark](label-dark.png), [plaque light](plaque-light.png) / [dark](plaque-dark.png).
- **Every door is drawn by the world behind it.** `sign(stage, theme)` is a method on the *child*: [Worlds](/imagine/scenes/worlds/) hangs three arches in Dawn/Dusk/Deep's own accents, [Plinth](/imagine/scenes/plinth/) a plinth cycling its mesh, [Quarters](/imagine/scenes/quarters/) a plate lifting one corner, [Gallery](/imagine/scenes/gallery/) three of its own paintings turning. A portal cannot go stale or lie about what it opens.
- **A fourth grain: [the gallery](/imagine/scenes/gallery/).** Four paintings drawn with the ordinary 2D canvas API and hung on planes — no image files, no fetches. Click one and *nothing in the room is rebuilt*: the picture's page claims `slot: "spot"`, which holds one spotlight, and declares a camera off the wall. The smallest swap there is — only where you stand changes. ![clicked a painting](gallery-click-filled.png)
- **Light and sky.** A key **and a rim** (one key over a pale world leaves every silhouette the same value as its background — that is what "reserved" looks like); one shadow-casting light per scene, opted in; per-world fog with a `near` you can push past the subject; a painted gradient dome for the tinted worlds and a `light-dark()` CSS gradient for the theme-anchored ones. Moods: [foyer](foyer-1920.png) / [dark](foyer-dark-1920.png) - [crossroads](worlds-1920.png) / [dark](worlds-dark-1920.png) - [Dawn](dawn-1920.png) - [Dusk](dusk-1920.png) - [Deep](deep-1920.png) - [plinth](plinth-1920.png) / [dark](plinth-dark-1920.png) - [quarters](quarters-1920.png) / [dark](quarters-dark-1920.png) - [gallery](gallery-1920.png) / [dark](gallery-dark-1920.png) - [a painting filled](gallery-motes-1920.png). Widths: [400](foyer-400.png) - [3440](foyer-3440.png).

**Verified headless** (SwiftShader WebGL): 19 urls, **zero console errors, zero HTTP 4xx, no horizontal overflow**, one name plate per link everywhere. Clicked the Gallery door in 3D, then a painting: url, slot map and camera all moved, back restored, and a **cold load of the deep url matched the clicked state EXACTLY** (url, path bar, slots, eye, aim, note, nav row). Leaving freezes the loop (`running: false`, frames 69 -> 69 across three seconds).

**Found and fixed while measuring: a texture leak.** A shadow map is a render target hanging off `light.shadow` with no geometry and no material, so `Stage.dispose()` never saw it - 40 swaps went 11 -> 31 textures. `Light.dispose()` in the traversal; the same 40 swaps now round-trip to exactly 33 geometries / 10 textures / 8 programs.

**Left:** labels do not scale with the canvas, so at 400 a name is a few pixels and the 2D nav row carries them (a screen-space size would cost a per-frame pass); the lands still ignore light/dark on purpose - a land *is* its palette; hover still lights a whole linked group; `Scene.js` is 550 lines and the 2D kit inside it is a real seam if it grows again. Not mine, seen while probing: `/imagine/feeds/data/feeds.css` 404s on every page under `/imagine/feeds/`.
